query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small percentage of nickel to HfZrTi high-entropy alloy will improve its ductility and toughness.
generation.conditions: Controlled environment with consistent temperature and pressure during alloying process
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary structure and phase distribution
generation.mechanism: Nickel enhances the ductility by promoting a more favorable grain boundary structure and reducing brittleness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased ductility and toughness in the HfZrTi HEA compared to the baseline without nickel.
generation.baseline: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy without nickel addition
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific composition of HfZrTi HEA and the percentage of nickel added.
generation.uncertainty: The exact percentage of nickel required for optimal improvement in ductility and toughness is unknown.

falsification_experiment.design: Create two sets of HfZrTi HEA samples, one with nickel and one without, and subject them to tensile testing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ductility and toughness of the nickel-added sample are not significantly higher than the baseline sample, the hypothesis is falsified.
